title: Fiberwise right adjoints assemble relative to a cocartesian base
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations and mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], enlarged if necessary. Let $p:E\to S$ and $q:D\to S$ be cocartesian fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $F:E\to D$ be a functor over $S$ preserving cocartesian edges. Suppose for every vertex $s$ the fiber functor $F_s:E_s\to D_s$ is equipped with a right adjoint $R_s$. There is a right adjoint $R:D\to E$ over $S$, with coherent unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_E\to RF$, counit $\varepsilon:FR\to\mathrm{id}_D$ and triangle homotopies over the identity of $S$. Its restriction to each fiber agrees, up to equivalence of adjunction data, with the specified fiber adjunction. In particular, the natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(Fx,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_E(x,Ry)$$
is over $\operatorname{Map}_S(p(x),q(y))$ and restricts to an equivalence on the homotopy fiber over every base arrow. The forward map is $k\mapsto R(k)\eta_x$ and the inverse is $h\mapsto\varepsilon_yF(h)$. These assertions and the adjunction data remain valid after pullback along every functor $S'\to S$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.2.6, opposite-category dual, applied to cocartesian fibrations and a cocartesian-edge-preserving functor; Definition 7.3.2.2, Remark 7.3.2.4 and Proposition 7.3.2.5 for relative adjunction and base change, printed pp. 1290-1292. Read online; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Fix a universe large enough to contain $S,E,D$ and their functor categories. For $y\in D_t$ put $r_y=R_t y$ and let $e_y:F(r_y)\to y$ be the specified fiber counit, hence an edge over $\mathrm{id}_t$. For $x\in E_s$ and $\alpha:s\to t$, choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $a:x\to x_\alpha$ by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Its image $F(a)$ is $q$-cocartesian by hypothesis. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], these horn-cocartesian lifts satisfy the mapping-square hypothesis for pointwise transport, for both $p$ and $q$. Apply the $K=\Delta^0$ mapping-fiber clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to these two lifts. With $\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha}$ denoting the homotopy fiber over $\alpha$, it identifies the map induced by $u\mapsto e_yF(u)$ with
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha}_E(x,r_y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{E_t}(x_\alpha,R_t y)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Map}_{D_t}(F_t x_\alpha,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha}_D(Fx,y).$$
The middle arrow is the given fiber adjunction, with inverse $k\mapsto R_t(k)\eta^t_{x_\alpha}$. This is the claimed map on homotopy fibers: precomposition by $F(a)$ sends $e_yF(v)$ to $e_yF(v)F(a)=e_yF(va)$. Thus the equivalence is for every base arrow, including all its higher homotopies, and uses no preservation of cocartesian edges by the proposed right adjoint.

source.place: Paragraph 2, mapping-complex adjunction; agent expansion of the opposite of HA Proposition 7.3.2.6: universal counit on each mapping-space fiber.

proof.text: For each $x,y$ the map $\Psi^y_x:u\mapsto e_yF(u)$ is a map over the identity of $\operatorname{Map}_S(s,t)$. Step 1 and [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], with its base equivalence the identity, imply that it is an equivalence on total mapping spaces. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] with $T=F$ and $\mathcal D_0=D$ to obtain $R^0:D\to E$, $\epsilon^0:FR^0\to\mathrm{id}_D$, and its coherent-diagram mapping equivalences. For each $y$, the universal pair $(R^0y,\epsilon^0_y)$ is equivalent to $(r_y,e_y)$: the two universal properties give arrows between their representing objects compatible with the two counits; applying those same equivalences to their composites gives the two inverse homotopies. In particular there is an equivalence $c_y:R^0y\to r_y$ with $e_yF(c_y)\simeq\epsilon^0_y$. Applying $q$ gives $q\epsilon^0_y\simeq p(c_y)$, since $qe_y=\mathrm{id}_t$. Consequently $\theta=q\epsilon^0:pR^0\to q$ has equivalence components and is a natural equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. This step does not assert that the initially assembled counit is already over the identity.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent realization of the finite adjunction; agent universal-arrow assembly and verification of its base equivalence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $p$, with shape $K=D$, diagram $R^0$, base diagram $q$, and transformation $\theta:pR^0\to q$. It supplies $\lambda:R^0\to R$ over $\theta$, with $pR=q$ and cocartesian components. Each $\lambda_y$ is an equivalence. Indeed, put $M=\operatorname{Map}_E(R^0y,z)$, $U=\operatorname{Map}_S(qy,pz)$ and $W=\operatorname{Map}_S(pR^0y,pz)$. Precomposition by $\theta_y$ gives an equivalence $g:U\to W$, with inverse induced by an inverse edge and its inverse homotopies. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], $\operatorname{Map}_E(Ry,z)$ is the homotopy pullback of $M\to W\leftarrow U$. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to compare this span with $M\to W\xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}}W$, using the equivalences $\mathrm{id}_M,g,\mathrm{id}_W$ on its three objects. The latter path-space pullback projects equivalently to $M$: its fiber is the space of paths starting at the image of a fixed point of $M$ and having a free endpoint, contracted to the constant path. This comparison commutes with projection to $M$, so precomposition by $\lambda_y$ is an equivalence for every $z$. For completeness, an edge $b:u\to v$ inducing equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(v,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(u,z)$ for every $z$ is invertible: use $z=u$ to obtain $a:v\to u$ with $ab\simeq1_u$; injectivity on components for $z=v$ then gives $ba\simeq1_v$ from $(ba)b\simeq b$. These are inverse witnesses under [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Componentwise equivalences give that $\lambda$ is a natural equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent adjunction maps; agent normalization of the right adjoint over the base, using the dual of HTT Proposition 3.1.2.1.

proof.text:
The components of $F\lambda:FR^0\to FR$ are $q$-cocartesian because $F$ preserves cocartesian edges. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] for $q$ and shape $D$, this is a cocartesian lift of $\theta$ in the functor category. Its mapping-fiber equivalence, with target diagram $\mathrm{id}_D$ in the fiber over $q$, lifts the point $\epsilon^0$ over $\theta$ to a coherent transformation $\epsilon:FR\to\mathrm{id}_D$ in that fiber, together with $\epsilon\circ F\lambda\simeq\epsilon^0$ over $\theta$. Thus $\epsilon$ is over $\mathrm{id}_q$. For every shape $K$ and diagrams $A:K\to E$, $B:K\to D$, the map
$$\Psi_K:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(A,RB)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(FA,B),\quad u\longmapsto(\epsilon B)F(u)$$
is an equivalence: the coherent-diagram equivalence for $(R^0,\epsilon^0)$ from [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] factors as $\Psi_K$ after postcomposition by $\lambda B$. Here the relevant functor categories are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Postcomposition by $\lambda B$ is an equivalence on their mapping spaces: postcompose with its inverse for an inverse map, using the inverse and composition homotopies of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. The factorization is the displayed counit homotopy whiskered by $B$, so it is coherent and natural in $A,B,K$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, specified coherent counit; agent factorization through cocartesian transport and coherent-diagram adjunction formula.

proof.text:
Since $F,R,\epsilon$ are over $S$, $\Psi_K$ commutes with projection to
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)}(pA,qB)$$
by $q((\epsilon B)F(u))=p(u)$. By [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] its restriction over every point of this base mapping space is an equivalence. In particular take $K=E$, $A=\mathrm{id}_E$, $B=F$, and the point $\mathrm{id}_p$. The inverse image of $\mathrm{id}_F$ is a coherent unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_E\to RF$ over $\mathrm{id}_p$, with $\epsilon F\circ F\eta\simeq\mathrm{id}_F$ over $\mathrm{id}_p$. These homotopy-fiber statements represent transformations and homotopies in the degreewise fiber, rather than merely transformations with a separately specified base path: apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with the identity base transformation and its identity lift. The identity lift is cocartesian because its mapping-space square is an identity square, by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. All shapes used here fit after the allowed universe enlargement.

source.place: Paragraph 2, units and counits and the following triangle-identity sentence; agent extraction of the unit in the fiber over the identity.

proof.text:
The other triangle homotopy is also vertical. Apply $\Psi_D$ from Steps 4-5 to $A=R$, $B=\mathrm{id}_D$, in the fiber over $\mathrm{id}_q$. Naturality of $\epsilon$ and the first triangle give
$$\Psi_D(R\epsilon\circ\eta R)=\epsilon\circ FR\epsilon\circ F\eta R\simeq\epsilon\circ\epsilon FR\circ F\eta R\simeq\epsilon=\Psi_D(\mathrm{id}_R).$$
Since this restricted $\Psi_D$ is an equivalence, this lifts to $R\epsilon\circ\eta R\simeq\mathrm{id}_R$ in the same fiber. The composition and inverse homotopies here are the canonical ones of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], applied also in functor categories. Now put $\Phi(k)=R(k)\eta_x$ and $\Psi(h)=\epsilon_yF(h)$. Naturality and the two vertical triangles give
$$\Psi\Phi(k)\simeq k\epsilon_{Fx}F\eta_x\simeq k,\qquad \Phi\Psi(h)\simeq R\epsilon_y\eta_{Ry}h\simeq h.$$
These are homotopies of maps of entire mapping spaces over $\operatorname{Map}_S(px,qy)$: whiskering and composition use coherent transformations, and every unit, counit and triangle used is vertical. They prove the stated forward and inverse formulas, with their base-arrow restrictions.

source.place: Paragraph 2, triangle identities; elementary naturality and two triangle calculations after Steps 4-5.

proof.text: Take $x,y$ over $s$ and restrict Step 5 at $K=\Delta^0$ to the base arrow $\mathrm{id}_s$. The mapping-fiber formula of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies the resulting spaces with $\operatorname{Map}_{E_s}(x,Ry)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{D_s}(F_sx,y)$; the restricted unit and counit and their triangles therefore give $F_s\dashv R|_{D_s}$. Both this counit and the specified counit for $F_s\dashv R_s$ are universal arrows for the same $F_s$. Apply the contractibility assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $F_s$ and all of $D_s$: it gives a coherent equivalence of right adjoints compatible with their counits. The units are the inverse images of the identity under the same coherent-diagram mapping equivalences, as in Step 5, so the comparison respects units and triangle homotopies as adjunction data. No compatibility of the initially specified adjunctions at different vertices was required.

source.place: Paragraph 2, comparison with the finite-level adjunction maps; agent uniqueness of the supplied fiber adjunction data.

proof.text: Let $a:S'\to S$ be any functor of quasicategories. In the degreewise pullbacks $E'=S'\times_SE$, $D'=S'\times_SD$, the functors $F,R$ induce $F',R'$ by acting on the second coordinate and fixing the first; the vertical transformations $\eta,\epsilon$ and their vertical triangle homotopies induce $\eta',\epsilon'$ in the same way. The pullbacks are quasicategories: first fill an inner horn in $S'$, then fill its image lifting problem using the inner-fibration part of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. For $x'\in E'$ and $y'\in D'$, put $\Phi'(k)=R'(k)\eta'_{x'}$ and $\Psi'(h)=\epsilon'_{y'}F'(h)$. Naturality of the pulled-back counit and the pulled-back first triangle give $\Psi'\Phi'(k)\simeq k\epsilon'_{F' x'}F'(\eta'_{x'})\simeq k$. Naturality of the pulled-back unit and the second triangle give $\Phi'\Psi'(h)\simeq R'(\epsilon'_{y'})\eta'_{R' y'}h\simeq h$. These are homotopies of maps on the whole mapping spaces by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] in the pullback quasicategories. Each factor fixes the first coordinate, so both homotopies are over $\operatorname{Map}_{S'}$ and give the equivalences on each homotopy fiber. Thus the pulled-back data themselves give the asserted relative adjunction and its formulas. Restriction to a vertex of $S'$ is the fiber comparison of Step 7 for its image in $S$.
